answer: A farm can script a thousand names, but cannot easily fake where they are. Random peers send each identity a whisper probe at unpredictable times and record how fast its signal returns from several vantage points. That timing vector forms a ridge no scattered agent shares exactly. Puppets run from one rack answer in lockstep, with near-identical ridges, so the protocol caps total influence per timing cluster, however many names it spawns. To escape, an operator must place every puppet on separate infrastructure, making each extra identity cost machines and networks, not just keys.
